problemModel:
AI UI drift is NOT primarily a taste failure or a hallucination problem — it is a RETRIEVAL and STATE failure that masquerades as taste. Decompose every divergence into three orthogonal causes, each with a distinct fix:

(1) RETRIEVAL FAILURE (the dominant cause, ~70% of drift): The model never had the relevant fact in context. Tokens, existing components, and naming precedents are not retrievable because they were never loaded — task context fills the window first. Result: re-invention of `Button.tsx` vs `PrimaryButton.tsx`, or padding 16 emitted as a literal because the token was never visible. Fix = retrieval architecture (queryable manifest + mandatory retrieve-before-create). Larger context windows do NOT fix this; they defer it.

(2) STATELESS RE-INVENTION (cross-session): Each API call is a fresh inference with zero memory of prior calls. Button v1 (radius 6) at 11am and Button v2 (radius 8) at 2pm are mutually unaware. Fix = external persistent state (a Git-tracked manifest the agent queries every session). Prompting "be consistent" is performative without queryable prior state.

(3) SAMPLING VARIANCE (in-session, temperature>0): 15px vs 16px, #F0F0F0 vs #F5F5F5 are token-selection randomness, not decisions. Fix = temperature 0.0–0.2 for UI code + multi-sample consensus for high-stakes components.

TASTE vs RETRIEVAL is the load-bearing distinction. TASTE = choosing 12px from a valid range when no prior decision exists (legitimately free; resolve ONCE at the system/token level, then it stops being taste). RETRIEVAL = choosing 12px, then 16px for the same role without checking what was chosen before (a fact was omitted that existed). Conflating these produces the canonical wrong fix: bloating prompts with "be consistent and tasteful" exhortations that address neither the missing index nor the missing state. The framework's job is to collapse taste into a finite set of pre-made decisions (tokens + components + variants-as-enums) so that at generation time there is nothing left to taste — only facts to retrieve. Hardcoded literals are then revealed as cost-optimized outputs of a system that failed to make the token cheaper to emit than the literal.
coreThesis: Design consistency is a retrieval-and-state problem disguised as a taste problem: make the right value cheaper to retrieve than to invent, persist every decision in one machine-queryable manifest that spans web and SwiftUI, gate creation behind mandatory retrieval, and the same independent agents will converge on the same UI — which a four-part composite score then proves.

frameworkPillars.name: One manifest, two emitters (single source of truth)
frameworkPillars.rationale: Cross-session and cross-stack drift both stem from the absence of shared external state. A platform-agnostic manifest is the only artifact that lets a React agent and a SwiftUI agent reuse the SAME decisions. It must be machine-optimized (queryable, indexed) first and human-readable second — prose specs exhaust the context window and are unparseable.
frameworkPillars.mechanics: A single DTCG-superset JSON (`design-system.json`) holds primitives→semantic→component token layers plus a component registry. Platform transform rules live as DATA (not code) inside the manifest: web→[name/kebab, color/hex, dimension/rem]→CSS vars + Tailwind @theme + TS types; swift→[name/camelCase enum-static, color/AssetCatalog, dimension/CGFloat]→`DS.swift` enum + `.xcassets`. WEB: tokens resolve to `var(--color-action-primary)` / Tailwind `@theme` utilities; components resolve to a shadcn-style registry-item. SWIFT: scalar tokens→`enum DS.Spacing { static let md: CGFloat = 16 }`, semantic colors→Asset Catalog ColorSet + `extension ShapeStyle where Self == Color`, cascading values (theme/density)→`@Entry` EnvironmentValues, component variants→`ButtonStyle` with an enum Variant. Codegen output is gitignored; the JSON is the source. CI regenerates and validates all platform outputs from the JSON on every change.

frameworkPillars.name: Retrieve-before-create, structurally enforced
frameworkPillars.rationale: Soft guidance ('reuse existing components') fails under task pressure — agents revert to invention. Retrieval must be a hard precondition, not a courtesy. This is the single highest-leverage convergence mechanism: it eliminates synonym bloat (Card/CardWrapper/c-card) by forcing a similarity check before any new artifact exists.
frameworkPillars.mechanics: A `query_manifest({intent, category?, platform?, limit?})` tool is a first-class capability. The harness tool-call validator FORBIDS `create_component` unless `query_manifest` was called earlier in the same session. WEB: query returns existing registry items with import paths, props, anti-patterns, and token requirements to paste as reference. SWIFT: query returns existing ViewModifiers/Styles/DS tokens with source locations. If top match ≥ 0.78 cosine similarity → REUSE/adapt and log the match; if < 0.78 → create new, but only as a registered, first-class artifact (never an inline special case), with a justification logged.

frameworkPillars.name: Mechanical constraint over exhortation
frameworkPillars.rationale: Literals are emitted because nothing forbade them and they were cheaper than tokens. Consistency must be the path of least resistance and deviation must be awkward. 'Be consistent' is a no-op; a lint gate that fails the build is not.
frameworkPillars.mechanics: Hard system-prompt constraints: 'NEVER emit raw px/hex/shadow/font-size literals; reference tokens only; if no token exists, ask before generating.' Generation config pinned to temperature 0.1–0.2 (0.0 for token/color name references). Variants modeled as ENUMS, not free parameters, on BOTH stacks (React discriminated-union `variant` prop; SwiftUI `enum Variant`) so there is no arbitrary-size argument to pass. Post-generation lint gates: WEB = stylelint-declaration-strict-value + an ESLint token-adherence rule (reject literal px/hex in style positions); SWIFT = SwiftLint `no_magic_numbers` + custom_rules regex banning `padding(\d+)`, `cornerRadius(\d+)`, `Color\.(red|blue|green)`, `.font(.system(size:`. Pre-commit + CI fail on violations not present in the decision log.

frameworkPillars.name: Register-after-create + decision log (no orphans, no silent fixes)
frameworkPillars.rationale: A created component invisible to the manifest is re-invented next session — the orphan problem. And an intentional off-scale value silently 'fixed' by a later audit is the 'why did my workaround get deleted' trap. Both are solved by making registration automatic and exceptions first-class.
frameworkPillars.mechanics: On create: deterministically compute `id = sha256(intent_keywords + signature_fingerprint + platform)[:16]`, extract intent keywords, append to manifest with metadata (agent-id, timestamp, source-location, status='NEW'), rebuild indices, then require user confirmation before commit. Two agents independently building 'primary button 48px' compute the SAME id → collision detected at registration → propose merge, not fork. Intentional exceptions go in `decision-log.json` ({decision-id, component-id, exception-type, justification, status}); the audit/refactor path MUST query it before proposing any change and surface the logged reason instead of auto-fixing.

frameworkPillars.name: Measurable convergence (the score closes the loop)
frameworkPillars.rationale: A consistency framework that cannot be measured cannot be tuned or trusted. The composite score is both the acceptance test for the harness and the longitudinal drift detector in CI — it turns 'looks consistent' into a number that gates merges and proves the framework works across the two stacks.
frameworkPillars.mechanics: Four AST-based sub-metrics (token-adherence, component-reuse, value-clustering, cross-session convergence) computed by stack-specific parsers — Babel/@babel/parser + postcss for React/CSS/Tailwind, SwiftSyntax for SwiftUI — compared against the same manifest. Sub-scores reported separately (radar chart) plus a single 0–100 composite. Any sub-score < 60 is flagged regardless of composite. CI gate fails merges below threshold (default 75) and emits remediation hints ('replace padding(16) with DS.Spacing.md').

manifestDesign:
SINGLE FILE: `design-system.json`. DTCG-superset (uses `$value`/`$type`/`$description`, curly-brace refs `{group.token}`), extended with a component registry, platform transforms, indices, and metadata. This is the ONE source of truth both stacks and the scorer read.

TOP-LEVEL SHAPE:
{
  "$schema": "...", "manifestVersion": "1.0", "metadata": {version, lastUpdated, lastUpdatedBy, gitCommit, sourceOfTruthUrl, namingConvention},
  "tokens": { "primitives": {...}, "semantic": {...}, "composite": {...}, "component": {...} },
  "components": [ ...registry entries... ],
  "platforms": { "web": {transforms:[...], target:"css-vars|tailwind-v4"}, "swift": {transforms:[...], target:"enum+assetcatalog"} },
  "indices": { "byCategory": {...}, "byIntent": {...}, "byPlatform": {...}, "semanticVectors": {tokenId: "sha256-fingerprint"} },
  "decisionLog": [ ...exceptions... ]
}

TOKEN LAYERING (3 tiers + composites, refs enforced one-directionally):
- primitives: raw brand-agnostic values, NO refs. e.g. `"blue-500": {"$value":"#0066cc","$type":"color","$description":"Raw brand blue"}`, `"space-4":{"$value":"16px","$type":"dimension"}`.
- semantic: role-based, MUST ref a primitive (parser REJECTS semantic→semantic refs to forbid hidden layers). e.g. `"color.action.primary":{"$value":"{blue-500}","$type":"color","$description":"Primary interactive surface; must hit WCAG AA on color.bg.surface"}`.
- composite: ONE token with object $value (typography{fontFamily,fontSize,fontWeight,lineHeight,letterSpacing}, border{color,width,style}, shadow{x,y,blur,spread,color}). Sub-values MUST be refs, not hardcoded (shadow.color:{color.shadow.default}, never #000).
- component: component-scoped, refs semantic/composite only. e.g. `"button.primary.background":{"$value":"{color.action.primary}"}`.
$description answers WHY/WHERE, never restates the name (reject tautologies like 'primary primary color').

COMPONENT REGISTRY ENTRY (extends shadcn registry-item with the agentic fields existing systems lack — purpose, anti-patterns, relationships, when-to-use, a11y, tokenMap). Minimum required fields the validator enforces: id, canonicalName, purposeStatement, variants, antiPatterns, importOrSource, tokenMap. Full entry:
{
  "id": "sha256(intent+signature+platform)[:16]",
  "canonicalName": "Button", "intentKeywords": ["action","submit","cta"],
  "category": "button/primary",                          // template {category}/{variant}/{modifiers}, NOT free-form
  "purposeStatement": "Triggers an action; NOT navigation (use Link).",  // semantic intent, not a label
  "whenToUse": [{scenario, code, preferredComponent, whyNotAlternative}],
  "variants": [{name:"variant", values:["primary","secondary","danger"], type:"enum"}],
  "variantCombinations": {"invalid":[{"disabled":true,"loading":true}]},  // interaction matrix
  "antiPatterns": [{pattern:"two primary buttons side-by-side", reason, correctAlternative, severity:"must-not|should-not|deprecated"}],
  "relationships": {parentContexts:[...], incompatibleWith:[ids], requiredNeighbors:[...]},
  "a11y": [{attribute, value, required, variants}],
  "tokenMap": {"primary": ["button.primary.background","spacing.inset.md","radius.sm"]},  // tokens each variant requires
  "platform": "web|swift",
  "web": {importPath:"@/components/ui/button", files:[{path,type}], cssVars:{...}},
  "swift": {source:"DS/Buttons.swift:48", style:"DSButtonStyle", construct:"DSButton(...)"},
  "createdBy", "createdDate", "status":"stable|new|experimental|deprecated",
  "embeddingFingerprint": "sha256(...)",                 // hash, NOT full vector (keeps file <50KB)
  "decisionLogRefs": [decision-ids]
}

WEB MAPPING: tokens → CSS custom properties (`--color-action-primary`) AND/OR Tailwind v4 `@theme` (auto-utilities), plus TS type export; components → registry items consumed via MCP/import. SWIFT MAPPING: scalar tokens → `enum DS.Spacing { static let md: CGFloat = 16 }`; semantic colors → Asset Catalog ColorSet (Any+Dark appearances, auto dark-mode) surfaced via `extension ShapeStyle where Self == Color { static var dsActionPrimary }`; cascading tokens (theme/density) → `@Entry var dsTheme` in EnvironmentValues; component variants → `ButtonStyle`/`LabelStyle` with `enum Variant`. Codegen (Style Dictionary / SwiftTokenGen) emits both targets from this JSON; generated code is gitignored, the JSON is canonical, CI asserts generated==manifest. VALIDATION (eager, at parse time before any codegen): every token has $type+$value; all refs resolve; no circular refs; composites have required sub-keys; semantic refs only primitives; component refs only semantic/composite; names match declared convention; every component has the minimum required fields.
metricDesign:
COMPOSITE = 0.40·TA + 0.30·CR + 0.20·(VC·100) + 0.10·(CC·100), single 0–100. Default weights; tunable per org (token-critical → TA 50–60; reliability-critical → CC 20–25; document rationale). Report all four sub-scores separately; flag any sub-score < 60 even if composite passes. Tiers: 0–50 poor, 50–75 developing, 75–90 mature, 90–100 excellent. Toolchain: React/CSS via @babel/parser + @babel/traverse + postcss/postcss-scss (already in harness deps); SwiftUI via SwiftSyntax; all compared to the same `design-system.json`. Canonicalize values before any comparison (#FF0000=rgb(255,0,0)=red→lowercase hex; padding(16)=.padding(16)=padding(.md); aggressive whitespace/identifier normalization).

(1) TOKEN-ADHERENCE (TA), 0–100, weight 0.40:
  TA = (token_references / styleable_declarations) × 100.
  DENOMINATOR = every declaration where a token COULD apply: color, background, border-color, spacing (padding/margin/gap), font-size, font-weight, line-height, border-radius, box-shadow, transition, plus SwiftUI padding/frame/cornerRadius/foregroundStyle/font.
  NUMERATOR = declarations referencing a DEFINED manifest token (`var(--…)`, Tailwind token-utility, `DS.Spacing.md`, `.dsActionPrimary`). Raw literals that match no token = numerator 0.
  EXCLUDED from denominator (documented ruleset): `auto`, `0`, `inherit`, `currentColor`, unitless z-index/flex/opacity, vendor prefixes.
  TYPE-CHECK GUARD (closes the 'spacing token used for a color' false-pass): a reference only counts if its token $type matches the property family (color prop must ref color token, spacing prop must ref dimension token). Mismatch counts as a violation.

(2) COMPONENT-REUSE (CR), 0–100, weight 0.30:
  CR = (reused_instances + variation_reuses) / (total_instances + missed_opportunities) × 100.
  reused_instances = JSX elements / SwiftUI Views matching a registered component name. variation_reuses = same base component + explicit registered overrides (NOT penalized — intentional variants are fine). missed_opportunities = clone-detected groups: 3+ instances with near-identical AST structure (< 15% tree-edit distance) that are NOT a registered component (the synonym-bloat signal). Use semantic similarity (prop signature + behavior), not string match, to avoid false clone flags. Requires manifest component inventory as baseline.

(3) VALUE-CLUSTERING (VC), 0–1 (×100 in composite), weight 0.20:
  Per dimension d: efficiency_d = min(unique_values_observed_d, defined_tokens_d) / unique_values_observed_d. (If 5 spacing tokens defined and 12 distinct spacing values observed → 5/12 = 0.417.) Strip media-query/responsive variants and cluster by INTENT before counting (so responsive 16px-mobile/24px-desktop is not double-penalized).
  VC = weighted avg across dimensions: colors 0.30, spacings 0.30, typography 0.20, radii 0.10, shadows 0.10.

(4) CROSS-SESSION CONVERGENCE (CC), 0–1 (×100), weight 0.10:
  Run the SAME prompt N≥3 (recommend 5) independent times. Normalize each output (identifiers, whitespace, formatting — MANDATORY first, else naming-only diffs tank an otherwise-converged set). Extract styled value-selections per run. CC = Krippendorff's Alpha over the per-decision token/value selections across runs = (observed_agreement − expected_random_agreement)/(1 − expected_random_agreement). < 0.60 → flag for manual review (output too non-deterministic). Because N runs are costly, sample CC on a cadence (1–2 sprints/month), not every commit; accept single-run variance between samples.

CAVEAT baked into reporting: high composite is necessary but NOT sufficient for visual correctness — pair with screenshot/visual-regression for pixel fidelity; validate scores against human design review and retune weights if a high score meets poor UX feedback.
convergenceProtocol:
The protocol is the system prompt AS a numbered, gated operational sequence (not advisory preamble), backed by harness tool-gating so it cannot be skipped:

STEP 0 — LOAD STATE: Read `design-system.json` + `decision-log.json` FIRST, before any generation. (Tool-gated: generation tools disabled until manifest is loaded this session.)
STEP 1 — RETRIEVE: Call `query_manifest({intent, category?, platform?})`. Score every candidate by cosine similarity to the new intent embedding. (Tool-gated: `create_component` FORBIDDEN unless `query_manifest` was called first in this session — the harness tool-call validator enforces ordering.)
STEP 2 — REUSE-vs-CREATE GATE: If top match ≥ 0.78 → REUSE the closest match (adapt via registered overrides only); log {matched-to-id, similarity, adaptation}. If < 0.78 → proceed to create, but record WHY the closest match was insufficient.
STEP 3 — ORDER OF OPERATIONS for any styling: match intent → reuse component → if styling needed, SNAP every value to the nearest `DS.*`/semantic token → only then create, and only as a first-class registered Style/Modifier/registry-item. NEVER emit a raw literal or an inline one-off variant.
STEP 4 — NAMING DETERMINISM: names follow the enforced template `{category}/{variant}/{modifiers}` (enum/dropdown selection, not free-form). IDs are `sha256(intent_keywords + signature_fingerprint + platform)[:16]` — content-derived, NOT uuid/sequential — so two independent agents building the same logical component compute the SAME id and the SAME file/name, which is what makes convergence mechanical rather than hoped-for.
STEP 5 — COLLISION → MERGE: Before appending, look up the computed id in `indices.byId`. If it exists, diff source/metadata and propose MERGE (union of source-locations) or an explicit VARIANT — never a silent fork.
STEP 6 — REGISTER LOOP: Auto-generate the manifest entry + decision-log entry, append, rebuild indices; require user confirmation before commit (default action = register; reject → roll back or mark experimental). No created artifact is ever invisible to the next session.
STEP 7 — EXCEPTIONS: Any deliberate off-scale value is logged in `decision-log.json` with a templated justification (platform-specific-override | temporary-workaround | legacy-compat | measured-perf). The audit path MUST query this log and surface the reason rather than auto-fixing.
STEP 8 — VARIANCE CONTROL: temperature 0.1–0.2 (0.0 for token/name references); for high-stakes shared components, multi-sample N=3–5 and return the output with highest semantic similarity to existing manifest entries.

Why this converges independent agents: identical content-hashed IDs + enforced naming template + mandatory same-manifest retrieval + reuse threshold means two agents on the same task, in different sessions, on different stacks, deterministically land on the same tokens, the same component id, and the same names — and the CC sub-metric measures exactly how well that holds.
openQuestions: Embedding determinism vs portability: deterministic IDs need a fixed, versioned embedding model for intent fingerprinting — which model, and how do we re-key the manifest when it changes without invalidating every existing ID? Do we fall back to keyword-hash IDs to stay model-independent?

Cross-platform reuse semantics: when a web Button and a SwiftUI button serve the same intent, is that one logical component with two platform implementations (shared id) or two ids linked by an intent cluster? This decides whether CR can credit cross-stack reuse and how the byPlatform index partitions.

Reuse threshold calibration: 0.78 is a borrowed default; it must be empirically tuned per design system's intent-cluster density. What labeled dataset / harness experiment do we run to set it, and should it be per-category (buttons tighter than layouts)?

Convergence weight tension: CC at 10% may under-incentivize the very property the framework exists to produce, yet raising it penalizes legitimately diverse outputs and is expensive (N runs). Should CC instead be a gate (fail < 0.60) rather than a weighted contributor?

Manifest authority & sync: if designers own tokens in Figma (Tokens Studio export) and engineers own the component registry in code, which half is canonical and how do we prevent the multi-source-of-truth drift the research explicitly warns against — one CI-enforced pivot file, or a merge step with conflict resolution?

Type-check guard coverage for TA: matching property-family to token $type is clean for color/dimension but ambiguous for composites (a typography token sets size+weight+leading at once) — how do we score partial application of a composite without false violations?

SwiftUI clone detection at scale: tree-edit distance over SwiftSyntax ASTs for the CR missed-opportunity metric is expensive on large view hierarchies; do we need a cheaper structural fingerprint, and what edit-distance threshold is right for SwiftUI's modifier-chain idiom vs React JSX?

Decision-log lifecycle: who resolves 'active' exceptions, and how do we prevent the log from becoming a dumping ground that quietly legitimizes drift (every literal 'justified') — does it need expiry dates or periodic review gates?
